assessment.nobel_worthiness: Detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos in 2013, followed by evidence for TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane, opened neutrino astronomy as an observational discipline. The enabling concept, a kilometre-scale instrumented ice volume, is a decades-long detector achievement of the kind I know well from astroparticle work.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and drove IceCube and its predecessor AMANDA; Spiering is credited for pioneering large-volume neutrino telescope development and the early programme. Other early pioneers (for example the Baikal and DUMAND efforts) and the large collaboration complicate a three-person limit; a two-person award is defensible on the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation of the diffuse flux across channels and the multi-messenger TXS 0506+056 association give a robust discovery. Source identification is still partial, so the field is maturing rather than complete; timing is good.
uncertainties: Whether credit for the instrument concept should extend beyond the two credited names, for example to early Baikal/DUMAND leaders not in the supplied list.
Population-level origin of the diffuse flux remains unresolved; I rely on memory of the literature and have not verified details.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The BeppoSAX X-ray afterglow of GRB 970228 and the optical redshift measurements that followed settled the cosmological origin of gamma-ray bursts after three decades of debate. This is a decisive, easily explained result with a lasting impact on high-energy astrophysics, and it came directly from instrument capability (wide-field cameras with fast localisation).
assessment.attribution: Costa and Frontera led the BeppoSAX GRB monitor and wide-field camera localisation and afterglow detection; Kulkarni led the ground-based optical/radio follow-up establishing redshifts and the fireball picture. Other contributors (van Paradijs, Djorgovski, Metzger, Piro and others) are not in the supplied credit, so any three-person allocation leaves people out.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than twenty-five years of independent confirmation by Swift, Fermi and ground facilities, with a stable interpretation. Recognition is arguably overdue, so there is no prematurity concern.
uncertainties: Fair division of credit between the X-ray localisation team and the optical follow-up groups, and the omission of some key contributors.
Whether the committee views the prize as astrophysics-discovery or as instrument-driven.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The July 2012 observation of a Higgs-like boson at the LHC confirmed the last missing Standard Model particle and the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking. The science is of the highest importance and clarity, and ATLAS and CMS gave independent confirmation by design.
assessment.attribution: Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee were founding leaders and spokespersons of the CMS and ATLAS concepts and proposals, a reasonable if imperfect proxy for experimental leadership. The 2013 prize recognised the theory; the experiment is by nature a collective achievement of thousands, so any configuration reflects organisational leadership rather than a single discovery act. Accelerator and detector builders are also not represented.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and confirmed; couplings and properties have been measured with growing precision since 2012. Experimental recognition after the 2013 theory prize is timely but each year of delay tightens the question.
uncertainties: Whether recognising individual spokespersons fairly represents a collaboration of thousands and the LHC machine builders.
Whether the committee regards the experimental discovery as already honoured via the 2013 prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: WMAP delivered full-sky CMB anisotropy maps that fixed the age, geometry, composition and reionisation history of the Universe at percent-level precision and established the standard LambdaCDM model. The impact is lasting and fundamental, and the instrument design (differential radiometry with exceptional systematic control) is elegant.
assessment.attribution: Bennett as PI, Page as instrument and observational lead, and Spergel as principal cosmological analysis leader span the key roles. Other WMAP team members and the COBE and Planck teams complicate attribution, and COBE already received the 2006 prize.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature: confirmed and extended by Planck and ground and balloon experiments, with the standard cosmological model stable for twenty years.
uncertainties: Risk that the committee judges WMAP as a continuation of the COBE recognition and the 2019 cosmology prize.
Choice between WMAP and Planck leadership, which are outside the supplied credit list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, redefining the limits of timekeeping and enabling relativistic geodesy and searches for variation of constants and dark matter. Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's implementations are central, and the achievement is clear and quantifiable.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first clocks; Ye drove the best-performing strontium clocks and many applications. This is a clean two-person attribution, although Hall and Hansch (2005) and ion-clock groups have already been recognised for related work.
assessment.maturity: Mature: many independent laboratories confirm the performance, and a redefinition of the second is in preparation. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2005 (frequency comb) and 2012 (ion trap) prizes, and with the ion-clock community.
Jun Ye also appears on the thorium nuclear clock candidate, which could dilute his claim if both are considered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory predicted flat bands at the magic angle, and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene created a tunable platform for strongly correlated physics. It has spawned a very large field of moire materials and is among the most influential condensed-matter discoveries of the decade.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 theoretical prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the experimental discovery. Cao, Fatemi and colleagues, plus earlier twisted-bilayer experiments by other groups, are not credited, so the allocation is partly open; this three-name configuration is plausible.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups with rapidly evolving understanding. The nature of the superconductivity remains under debate, so the interpretation is not yet stable, and the discovery is somewhat premature by Nobel norms.
uncertainties: Origin of the superconducting pairing is unresolved.
Credit of the experimental team beyond the principal investigator, and whether the theory and experiment should be linked.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The first horizon-scale images of M87* and Sgr A* directly test general relativity in the strong-field regime and show black-hole shadows. A VLBI technology achievement at millimetre wavelengths, with a very clear public and scientific impact.
assessment.attribution: Doeleman led the EHT collaboration and the VLBI technical development; Falcke proposed the shadow imaging concept with Melia and Agol and was a leader in the science case. Zensus is a leading institutional figure but less decisive on the discovery. The collaboration is very large, and others such as Bower and the array builders contribute substantially.
assessment.maturity: Two independent targets and polarisation results support the images, but modelling choices and interpretation remain debated and further data are coming. Recognition is reasonable but slightly early.
uncertainties: Disputed or diffuse credit for a collaboration of hundreds, and the exclusion of conceptual and instrumental contributors.
Systematic uncertainties in image reconstruction and interpretation, which I know only from the literature.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Silicon microstrip and hybrid pixel detectors transformed particle tracking and vertexing and made modern LHC experiments, including Higgs measurements, possible. The reach extends to X-ray imaging and medical applications (Medipix). This is enabling technology of lasting influence, and I am particularly aware of its role in space and balloon instruments.
assessment.attribution: Parker developed silicon microstrip and 3D detector concepts, Heijne led early silicon strip and pixel work at CERN, and Campbell developed hybrid pixels (Medipix, Timepix). Other pioneers such as Kemmer, Hyams and Rancoita and the groups behind CMOS pixels are not credited, and attribution is distributed.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: technology adopted for decades across experiments, and recognised only partially through the Charpak prize of 1992 for a different detector class.
uncertainties: Whether detector instrumentation fits the committee's preference for discoveries or inventions, and whether the credit is sharp enough.
Many contributors; unresolved priority between microstrip, hybrid and monolithic pixel developments.
